What degraded

  • Not merged. CI exits 3 on the Grid Watch page check
    The large load queue reading stopped because ERCOT named the September overview without a year. The fix is gridwatch lane, one more candidate filename in scripts/gridwatch/queue_collect.py. Image links point at the run branch until the pull request merges.
  • Shipped at the round cap under the bar
    7.15 against an 8.0 top rung, the art median 6.5 under the 8.5 craft floor. Frame 4's robot arm was charged as a toy in every round.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Texas A&M plans an AI foundry for new alloys, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Why does an AI lab melt metal?

Several dozen elements make roughly a trillion possible mixes. That sounds like a job for software. Raymundo Arróyave of Texas A&M says no computational tool anywhere can predict how an alloy will behave.

A $2 million WoodNext Foundation grant will help build the Aggie AI Foundry. Computer controlled arms on an assembly line are to mix, melt and test new alloys. The university says existing self driving labs can't handle alloys at up to 3,000 degrees Celsius. Months of work cut to a week or less is the goal, not a result.

A separate NSF award has obligated $4.1 million of an estimated $24.9 million. It funds the open access Autonomous Robotic Metallurgist at Texas A&M.

The award record names researchers at non-R1 and EPSCoR institutions among its intended users. Who outside Texas A&M makes the first alloy there?

#TexasAM #AggieAIFoundry #NSF

The machine changed itself

  • Machine queue, seven items (commit 87b2cc78)
    The grade's quarter resolution bloom on a dark macro, a rig distance that puts the shadow camera's near plane at the target, a practical light that saturates its neighbours, an audition loop with no diagnostic step, the toy robot arm, the interior wall seam behind type, and the foundry's lab models for the kit.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

NOT MERGED. CI goes red on the Grid Watch page check, which exits 3 because the large load queue reading stopped: ERCOT published the September Monthly Operational Overview on October 16th without the year in its filename, and the collector builds the name with the year. That fix is in the gridwatch lane, which this run may not touch. One action clears it: add the yearless candidate filename to report_url in scripts/gridwatch/queue_collect.py, then merge this run's pull request once CI is green. The record: 165 items re-verified and stamped, 30 boundaries re-measured with the project's own agent (a browser user agent probe was refused by the classifier and not routed around), tx-2026-0218, tx-2026-0201, tx-2026-0055 and tx-2026-0182 updated. The deck: carousel no. 65, the Aggie AI Foundry. The three frame audition took sixteen art director readings, fifteen on the cover, each finding a real render defect (copper read as wood, then the grade's bloom, the shadow camera's near plane and a practical light, found by diagnostic renders). Three panel rounds: 6.75, 7.13, then 7.15 at the cap with no hard fail. The defect named in every round and never fixed is frame 4's robot arm, which reads as a toy. Prompt audit: 2,118 calls measured, 109 flagged, every one under twenty seconds. No-stall hook armed at 05:03:34 UTC, judged the session unattended, refused nothing.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
